Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-001 · Source record

C1 disposition. Retained product direction. R14 models a narrow service contract; complete enterprise capability catalogs remain unqualified. Related: RV-01
AP-ADR-001Make the AI Service Contract the primary product objectProposed
Area Product & experienceSuggested owner Platform product architectDate 8 October 2026

Context

Provider-centric administration makes users coordinate model names, policy attachments, keys and budgets without a single statement of what an application is allowed to rely on. The product needs a stable unit of ownership and change.

Alternatives considered

Expose provider endpoints directly; use loosely related gateway entities; or introduce a versioned service contract. Direct endpoints are simplest for one provider but transfer governance coordination to every application.

Proposed decision

Use a tenant-scoped, versioned AI Service Contract containing protocol, capability, quality, processing, financial and lifecycle requirements. Resolve qualified implementations behind it. Make the same object visible in the console, APIs, delivery tools, request evidence and cost attribution. Do not advertise cross-provider interchangeability beyond its tested contract.

Consequences and tradeoffs

This reduces configuration ambiguity but adds catalog and contract maintenance. Specialized provider APIs remain separate qualified contracts. A small single-provider application may correctly choose direct native access instead.

Required validation

Test whether users can identify owner, permissions, destinations and cost envelope from one service view. Run the same contract fixtures against each eligible target.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when the service abstraction loses required native semantics or creates more application exceptions than it removes.

Evidence [R08]

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-002 · Source record

C1 disposition. Partial local scope model. Tenant/workspace membership exists, but dedicated placement is not implied. Related: RV-07
AP-ADR-002Separate administrative hierarchy from physical placementProposed
Area Tenancy & securitySuggested owner Tenant platform leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Teams often confuse billing labels, workspaces and isolation boundaries. That confusion permits accidental cross-tenant joins and creates misleading promises about dedicated infrastructure.

Alternatives considered

Flat API keys; tenant equals namespace; or explicit organization/tenant/workspace/service resources with independent cell placement. A namespace alone cannot describe all security and recovery boundaries.

Proposed decision

Treat tenant as an authorization and financial boundary, workspace as organization/environment, and cell assignment as a placement and failure-isolation decision. Include verified scope in every resource aggregate, job and evidence record. Expose the isolation manifest rather than infer exclusivity from a product label.

Consequences and tradeoffs

More explicit identifiers and migrations are required. Tenant movement must reconcile state, keys, jobs and financial grants. A workspace cannot be moved across tenants by editing a billing tag.

Required validation

Enumerate cross-tenant negative tests for every API family and export. Verify cell assignment independently of labels, queue names and cost centers.

Revisit trigger

Revisit if business tenancy changes or a customer requires an additional legal or sovereign trust boundary.

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-003 · Source record

C1 disposition. Target only as independently deployed roles. R14 is a single-node Python application with local workers. Related: RV-01 RV-02 RV-05
AP-ADR-003Start with a modular control plane and four deployable rolesProposed
Area Architecture & runtimeSuggested owner Platform engineering leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

A large microservice architecture would add network failure modes before domain boundaries are proven. A single process for all functions would instead mix administrative authority, content handling and financial correctness.

Alternatives considered

One all-purpose binary; many small network services; or a modular control plane with separate execution and admission roles. Choose service boundaries for authority and recovery, not repository aesthetics.

Proposed decision

Package Control API and Control Worker from one modular Go codebase. Deploy Execution Kernel and Admission Service separately in each cell with narrowly scoped credentials. Keep catalog, tenant, compiler and change modules inside the control application until measured load or independent ownership justifies extraction.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Transactional control workflows stay simple, but module boundaries require discipline and independent tests. Execution and admission introduce a deliberate network dependency whose latency and availability must be qualified.

Required validation

Exercise each role with only its declared credentials. Verify an execution compromise cannot alter approvals and a control outage does not become an unbounded request-path dependency.

Revisit trigger

Revisit extraction when a module has independently measured scaling, security or release requirements.

Evidence Original design decision; evaluate against the stated acceptance gates.

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-004 · Source record

C1 disposition. RECONSIDER alongside RV-02. Go is a proposed runtime choice, not implemented or accepted. Qualify reuse of LiteLLM before selecting a replacement kernel. Related: RV-02
AP-ADR-004Use a small Go execution kernel with build-time adaptersProposed
Area Architecture & runtimeSuggested owner Runtime leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Repeated parsing across proxy scripts, callback layers and sidecars can produce conflicting semantics and retry ownership. A language rewrite alone does not prove an architectural improvement.

Alternatives considered

Extend an incumbent proxy; build a Rust kernel; or implement one typed Go kernel with constrained adapters. Existing ingress remains useful for transport without owning AI semantics.

Proposed decision

Use Go initially for kernel and control implementation. Parse each approved protocol once, retain a typed request view and execute one explicit plan. Ship reviewed adapters at build time. Use existing ingress for transport limits but disable independent provider retries. Optimize native hot paths only after profiling a qualified workload.

Consequences and tradeoffs

A common language lowers integration overhead but introduces garbage-collection and allocation considerations. Owning adapters creates a maintenance commitment; the capability matrix limits that commitment to supported combinations.

Required validation

Measure allocation, active streams, cancellation, serialization, connection reuse and p99 admission overhead under the reference load. Compare with an incumbent under identical policy settings.

Revisit trigger

Revisit the runtime language or adapter boundary only when reproducible measurements show a material bottleneck.

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-005 · Source record

C1 disposition. Candidate covers only plain-text nonstreaming Chat Completions. Other normalized/native protocols are not qualified. Related: RV-02
AP-ADR-005Qualify normalized and native APIs independentlyProposed
Area Architecture & runtimeSuggested owner API architecture leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Common request syntax does not establish common tool behavior, structured output, reasoning, resource ownership or billing semantics. Lossy translation can appear successful while breaking the application.

Alternatives considered

Universal normalization; unrestricted passthrough; or a small normalized contract plus explicitly approved native contracts. Both extremes obscure important constraints.

Proposed decision

Publish conformance per provider/account/model/version/endpoint/geography/capability tuple. Reject unsupported fields. Preserve approved provider-specific extensions without allowing endpoint or credential overrides. Native APIs use the same tenant and governance boundaries but have independent lifecycle and acceptance evidence.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The catalog becomes larger and support is deliberately bounded. Applications gain explicit incompatibility errors rather than silently degraded behavior. Some advanced features remain provider-bound.

Required validation

Test schemas, error details, streaming events, tools, context limits, usage and provider-owned IDs. Negative tests must prove that native routes do not bypass mandatory controls.

Revisit trigger

Revisit an abstraction when upstream protocol changes or an application needs a capability outside the existing contract.

Evidence [R08]

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-006 · Source record

C1 disposition. Partial local implementation plus optional OIDC. Enterprise IdP, workload identity and browser deployment still need qualification. Related: RV-07
AP-ADR-006Derive identity and scope from verified authorityProposed
Area Tenancy & securitySuggested owner Identity and security leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Client-supplied tenant labels, cost metadata and tool descriptions are not proof of authority. Human administration, application workloads and delegated end users need distinct lifecycles.

Alternatives considered

Shared API keys; caller-selected tenant headers; or short-lived verified identity with explicit scoped grants. Long-lived emergency keys remain an exception with recovery controls.

Proposed decision

Use OIDC for human access through a BFF and short-lived audience-bound workload credentials. Resolve tenant and grants server-side. Authenticate internal services with approved workload identity. Keep original end-user authorization distinct from gateway identity when calling retrieval or business tools.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Identity-provider and key-rotation integration are required. Cached verification material has bounded age. The platform must explain access failures without disclosing foreign resource existence.

Required validation

Test wrong issuer/audience, expiration, revoked grants, forged tenant metadata, provider-token reuse and cross-object access. Verify support access has an independent expiry and audit trail.

Revisit trigger

Revisit for new federation, delegated-user or sovereign trust requirements.

Related decisions AP-ADR-002 AP-ADR-008 AP-ADR-014 AP-ADR-025

Evidence [R11] [R15]

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-007 · Source record

C1 disposition. Proposed only. Pooled/dedicated/sovereign product editions are not delivered.
AP-ADR-007Offer pooled, dedicated and sovereign isolation explicitlyProposed
Area Tenancy & securitySuggested owner Infrastructure security architectDate 8 October 2026

Context

A tenant may need stronger isolation than row filtering, while smaller tenants benefit from shared infrastructure. Calling every topology dedicated obscures real exposure.

Alternatives considered

Only shared infrastructure; one complete installation per tenant; or graduated isolation using the same contract/API model. The choice should match risk and operations capacity.

Proposed decision

Define manifests for pooled cells, exclusive tenant cells and separate sovereign installations. State exclusivity for processes, nodes, networks, ledgers, keys, evidence and administrator access. Keep the service API consistent. Add dedicated cells only when requirements justify their cost.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Dedicated operation increases infrastructure and upgrade overhead. A dedicated runtime does not remove a shared management administrator from the threat model. Tenant movement becomes a controlled state migration.

Required validation

Inspect the actual infrastructure and credential boundary against the declared manifest. Run noisy-neighbor and cross-tenant tests on pooled operation and recovery drills on dedicated stores.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when threat classification, performance isolation or contractual geography changes.

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-008 · Source record

C1 disposition. Object-level checks are locally implemented. PostgreSQL/RLS is not implemented or qualified. Related: RV-07
AP-ADR-008Use object authorization plus database row-security defenseProposed
Area Tenancy & securitySuggested owner Data security leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Correct API scoping is essential but can regress in exports, joins or background tasks. Database protections provide a second boundary only when roles and pooling behavior are configured correctly.

Alternatives considered

Application filters only; per-tenant database everywhere; or object checks plus row security for pooled stores and separate databases for stronger isolation.

Proposed decision

Apply action/object authorization before queries and tenant-aware primary/foreign keys. Use non-owner application database roles without BYPASSRLS, enforce row policies where appropriate and set verified scope transaction-locally. Separate migration/owner credentials. Treat background jobs and exports as ordinary authorized callers.

Consequences and tradeoffs

RLS complicates administration and migrations, and it does not constrain privileged database owners. Pool leakage and unsafe session-setting interfaces must be tested explicitly. Dedicated databases remain available for stronger boundaries.

Required validation

Test foreign rows through every query family, transaction rollback, prepared statements, connection reuse and restore. Verify runtime roles cannot alter scope or policies through exposed SQL.

Revisit trigger

Revisit if a data store cannot express reliable scoped constraints or a tenant requires independent restoration.

Related decisions AP-ADR-002 AP-ADR-006 AP-ADR-027 AP-ADR-033

Evidence [R12]

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-009 · Source record

C1 disposition. Narrow local rules exist. General mandatory-policy compilation/intersection remains proposed.
AP-ADR-009Compose mandatory policy by intersection and explicit denyProposed
Area Tenancy & securitySuggested owner Policy architecture leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Last-writer configuration precedence permits a convenient child or request setting to weaken a parent control. Operators need one understandable effective policy.

Alternatives considered

Last setting wins; arbitrary plugin ordering; or a typed deny-preserving composition model. Flexibility that changes authority must be explicit rather than implicit precedence.

Proposed decision

Define policy fields with typed composition: intersect allowed sets, union denies, minimize maxima and maximize required floors. Requests can choose only within the result. Reject conflicting, unbounded or unsupported policies at compilation. Include provenance for every effective value and safe reason codes at evaluation.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Some provider options become unavailable until a contract explicitly delegates them. The compiler is security-critical and requires generated negative tests. Arbitrary policies are not exposed as an unrestricted UI editor.

Required validation

Property-test monotonicity over generated parent/child/request combinations, including absent, empty, wildcard and alternate-protocol cases.

Revisit trigger

Revisit only with a formal rule for new policy types that preserves mandatory authority.

Related decisions AP-ADR-001 AP-ADR-005 AP-ADR-010 AP-ADR-036

Evidence [R06] [R10]

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-010 · Source record

C1 disposition. Proposed only. Local reviewed-content fingerprints are not signed distributed policy bundles.
AP-ADR-010Distribute immutable signed contract bundles with bounded validityProposed
Area Architecture & runtimeSuggested owner Release security leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Hot configuration reloads are useful but can expose partial objects, untrusted updates or indefinitely stale grants. Request handling needs a consistent approved view.

Alternatives considered

Read the control database per request; permit direct runtime edits; or distribute signed immutable snapshots with explicit activation and expiry.

Proposed decision

Compile a complete artifact containing contracts, eligibility, policy, grant epoch, price references, validity and kernel compatibility. Verify signer, digest, schema, epoch and age before atomic activation. Retain one revision per in-flight admission and emit a cell receipt. Invalid updates never produce a permissive empty state.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Artifact distribution and trust-root rotation become operational responsibilities. Signed does not imply fresh or correct; expiry and authorization age can reduce outage availability.

Required validation

Inject altered, unsigned, expired, incompatible and downgraded artifacts. Test cold starts, clock skew, partial download and request concurrency during activation.

Revisit trigger

Revisit bundle granularity when cell size or update rates create measurable distribution cost.

Related decisions AP-ADR-009 AP-ADR-012 AP-ADR-013 AP-ADR-014

Evidence [R13]

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-011 · Source record

C1 disposition. Target ownership contract. LiteLLM settings ownership must be exposed and reconciled; no Git/IaC reconciler is implemented. Related: RV-06
AP-ADR-011Give configuration one declared owner across UI, Git and IaCProposed
Area Automation & deliverySuggested owner Developer experience leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Multiple configuration surfaces can overwrite each other and make incidents impossible to reconstruct. A familiar declarative tool must not bypass review.

Alternatives considered

File wins; database wins; last write wins; or explicit resource ownership with all writers using the same domain commands.

Proposed decision

Mark resources as Git-managed or API-managed and reject conflicting writes with an actionable source reference. Console, CLI, Terraform and Kubernetes integrations submit typed ChangeSets with base versions. Ownership transfer and emergency exceptions are themselves reviewed, expiring changes.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Users cannot freely edit every field in every interface. The product must explain the ownership source clearly and provide a legitimate transfer workflow. Drift becomes a first-class state.

Required validation

Submit conflicting writes through every interface, including emergency tooling. Verify no path mutates a runtime or database field outside the change protocol.

Revisit trigger

Revisit ownership granularity when teams need delegated field-level management with a provable conflict model.

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-012 · Source record

C1 disposition. Locally exercised independent service/workload/budget review. Local-operator egress/maintenance attestations are a different, weaker authority path.
AP-ADR-012Require independent approval of an exact immutable proposalProposed
Area Automation & deliverySuggested owner Governance ownerDate 8 October 2026

Context

A generic approval label does not show what was reviewed or whether the author could self-approve. Editing after review invalidates the meaning of approval.

Alternatives considered

Immediate updates; external ticket references; or approvals tied to a typed proposal digest and exact base resource versions.

Proposed decision

Freeze the ChangeSet at review, require a distinct authorized reviewer, and bind approval to its digest, scope, tests and expiry. Recheck authority and versions at release. Material edits create a new version. Financial expansion requires a permitted financial approver; higher-risk changes can require multiple disciplines.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Review adds friction for meaningful changes. Safe delegated actions must have explicit pre-approved envelopes rather than informal bypasses. Emergency authority is a separate time-limited protocol.

Required validation

Test self-approval, withdrawn grants, edited proposals, expired approvals, stale base versions and releases through alternate APIs.

Revisit trigger

Revisit review thresholds using measured operator burden and incident data, without removing digest binding.

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-013 · Source record

C1 disposition. Distinct states are retained. Synthetic/local observation is not proof of a healthy live model deployment. Related: RV-06
AP-ADR-013Distinguish desired, approved, active and healthy stateProposed
Area Automation & deliverySuggested owner Release engineering leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

An API save or orchestration acknowledgement does not prove that the intended configuration runs in every target cell. Green deployment labels can conceal partial application.

Alternatives considered

Treat save as success; display deployment tool status only; or model release distribution and runtime receipts independently.

Proposed decision

Record a release operation with target cells, approved digest, canary plan and observed receipts. Expose partial activation and health gates. Rollback constructs a new approved release against current mandatory policy; it does not rewrite history or revive revoked grants.

Consequences and tradeoffs

The UI needs more states and correlation identifiers, but they correspond to real distinctions. Old/new revisions may coexist during a canary, so each request records its exact contract.

Required validation

Partition a target cell, delay receipts, fail health checks and change policy during a rollback. Verify the console never labels incomplete activation as fully healthy.

Revisit trigger

Revisit rollout strategy as deployment scale and workload blast radius change.

Related decisions AP-ADR-010 AP-ADR-012 AP-ADR-014 AP-ADR-035

Evidence [R03]

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-014 · Source record

C1 disposition. Local grant/binding rechecks exist. Distributed epoch propagation and offline revocation bounds remain unproved.
AP-ADR-014Make revocation freshness an explicit availability tradeoffProposed
Area Tenancy & securitySuggested owner Security operations leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Last-known configuration can preserve availability during an outage but may continue authorizing access after revocation. The acceptable window depends on data sensitivity.

Alternatives considered

Online authorization for every request; indefinite cached grants; or bounded locally evaluated authorization with epochs and explicit stale behavior.

Proposed decision

Use monotonic authorization epochs and short-lived grants. Distribute revocations with high priority and report acknowledgement coverage. Restricted services stop new admission when the approved age bound expires; public services may use separately approved longer bounds. Existing work follows an explicit cancellation/exposure policy.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Partitions can intentionally deny otherwise valid requests. Shorter windows require more reliable distribution and clock management. Revocation cannot retroactively erase output or guarantee upstream cancellation.

Required validation

Test partitions, delayed updates, expired grants, clock skew, persisted snapshots and key rotation. Measure the actual worst-case continued-admission window.

Revisit trigger

Revisit freshness bounds through accountable data-owner approval and tested reliability tradeoffs.

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-015 · Source record

C1 disposition. SQLite local financial admission exists for synthetic requests. Candidate has an external Authority port; distributed strict guarantees are not proved. Related: RV-03 RV-04
AP-ADR-015Separate strict financial admission from analytics and rate limitsProposed
Area Finance & optimizationSuggested owner Financial systems leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Completed-usage counters and dashboards cannot prevent every concurrent dispatch that creates economic exposure. Capacity and provider token limits answer different questions from spending authorization.

Alternatives considered

Retrospective counters only; approximate local reservations; or an authoritative regional transactional admission service for strict workloads.

Proposed decision

Require a durable reservation before any bounded billable attempt. Maintain integer-currency account balances, idempotent identities, known settlement and unresolved exposure. Financial unavailability denies strict new work. Optional advisory-only budgets must be a separately labeled contract, never an automatic fallback.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Transactions add latency and can reduce availability or utilization. Unknown pricing requires rejection or an explicitly accepted risk envelope. The guarantee concerns admitted modeled exposure, not all possible provider invoice charges.

Required validation

Run synchronized near-limit admissions, duplicate requests, database failover, rollback and missing-usage tests. Verify conservation and absence of provider attempts without admission IDs.

Revisit trigger

Revisit implementation only with evidence that the replacement preserves authority under concurrency and failure.

Related decisions AP-ADR-016 AP-ADR-017 AP-ADR-018 AP-ADR-019

Evidence [R04] [R05]

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-016 · Source record

C1 disposition. Proposed only. No implemented regional spending-right allocation or multi-node reclamation. Related: RV-03
AP-ADR-016Partition regional spending rights and never reclaim by timeout aloneProposed
Area Finance & optimizationSuggested owner Distributed systems leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

A global financial ceiling is difficult to enforce with independently writable regional counters. Lease expiry does not prove that an isolated old spender stopped using its rights.

Alternatives considered

One synchronous global ledger; eventually consistent totals; or bounded regional grants with explicit transfer and fencing.

Proposed decision

Start with one writer region per financial account. Delegate nonoverlapping grants to cells only through a durable allocator. Reclaim rights after sealing, fencing and reconciling consumption and unknown attempts, not merely after elapsed lease time. Quarantine restored grants until current authority is established.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Rights may be stranded during a partition and regional recovery may require a write-off or additional separately approved funding. This deliberately favors conservation over perfect utilization.

Required validation

Model grant conservation and test split connectivity, stale writers, delayed settlement, duplicate transfer and snapshots restored after reallocation.

Revisit trigger

Revisit regional mobility only after formal and fault-injection evidence proves safe transfers.

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-017 · Source record

C1 disposition. Locally exercised durable intent and uncertainty. Live upstream attempt/idempotency behavior remains unqualified. Related: RV-03
AP-ADR-017Track logical intent, individual attempts and uncertain dispatchProposed
Area Architecture & runtimeSuggested owner Runtime reliability leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

One user request can generate several provider executions. Retrying after a timeout can duplicate both cost and side effects without the client knowing.

Alternatives considered

Untracked retries; global request IDs only; or a logical-request/attempt state machine with scoped idempotency.

Proposed decision

Use a tenant/service-scoped client intent key and material request hash. Assign an ID to each provider attempt. Durably mark possible dispatch before sending and distinguish known rejection, completed usage and unknown outcome. Do not claim provider idempotency unless the exact provider contract supplies it.

Consequences and tradeoffs

A crash around external dispatch can leave unresolved records. That is honest uncertainty, not an implementation failure to conceal. Recovery may be slower than blind retry.

Required validation

Crash before and after local commit, send, provider acceptance, first output and settlement. Replay same and changed payloads with one key.

Revisit trigger

Revisit attempt granularity when new tool, batch or stateful provider contracts are introduced.

Related decisions AP-ADR-005 AP-ADR-015 AP-ADR-018 AP-ADR-021

Evidence [R14]

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-018 · Source record

C1 disposition. Local unknown/settlement semantics exist. No provider billing join or external invoice reconciliation is implemented. Related: RV-03
AP-ADR-018Preserve unknown cost and reconcile with explicit adjustmentsProposed
Area Finance & optimizationSuggested owner FinOps ownerDate 8 October 2026

Context

Late usage, missing trailers, external account activity and invoice aggregation prevent perfect request-level billing in every integration. Zero is an incorrect representation of unknown.

Alternatives considered

Estimate and overwrite; release after timeout; or retain unresolved authority and maintain separate estimate, usage and invoice facts.

Proposed decision

Keep unknown outcomes reserved until reconciled or covered by an approved write-off. Record price/usage corrections as adjustments, not silent history edits. Match invoices at the provider-supported granularity and expose remaining differences and confidence. Require accountable review above delegated write-off thresholds.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Financial views are more complex than a single spend total. Some accounts can remain unresolved for a long period, and conservative exposure reduces usable allowance.

Required validation

Exercise missing usage, invoice-only charges, actual cost above estimate, zero-cost confirmed outcomes, duplicate settlement and account-level unmatched differences.

Revisit trigger

Revisit matching adapters and risk allowances when provider billing identifiers or contracts improve.

Related decisions AP-ADR-015 AP-ADR-016 AP-ADR-017 AP-ADR-019

Evidence Original design decision; evaluate against the stated acceptance gates.

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-019 · Source record

C1 disposition. Synthetic price revisions exist. A qualified real-provider worst-case estimator is still required. Related: RV-03 RV-04
AP-ADR-019Version prices and qualify the reservation estimatorProposed
Area Finance & optimizationSuggested owner FinOps engineering leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Rates, token categories, service tiers and ancillary charges can change independently of model names. An unversioned price lookup cannot explain a historic admission decision.

Alternatives considered

Hardcoded current prices; runtime web lookup; or approved versioned price books with estimator conformance.

Proposed decision

Include provenance, currency, effective dates and covered billing dimensions in the price book. Record its revision in every admission. Bound input, output, recovery and auxiliary service exposure. Reject strict routes with unknown upper-bound semantics unless an explicit risk allowance covers the uncertainty.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Price administration is a release responsibility. Conservative estimation can strand funds and dynamic provider behavior may prevent a complete bound. The system must surface exclusions plainly.

Required validation

Test integer arithmetic, currency rounding, token categories, cache rates, media units, tool charges, price transitions and missing catalog entries.

Revisit trigger

Revisit after provider billing changes or observed estimation error exceeds the accepted envelope.

Evidence Original design decision; evaluate against the stated acceptance gates.

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-020 · Source record

C1 disposition. Prototype/advisory only. Synthetic comparisons do not demonstrate production quality-adjusted savings.
AP-ADR-020Optimize only inside qualified capability and quality constraintsProposed
Area Finance & optimizationSuggested owner Model quality leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

The cheapest response is not necessarily the cheapest successful task. Behavioral, privacy and context differences can make a syntactically compatible fallback unsafe.

Alternatives considered

Lowest price; latency-only routing; or constrained eligibility followed by a measured cost/quality objective.

Proposed decision

First filter targets by authorization, processing geography, protocol/features, context and task-quality gates. Optimize only among eligible candidates. Store evaluation-set version and confidence. Produce reviewable recommendations; measure realized cost per accepted outcome after a controlled release.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Fewer targets may remain during an incident, reducing availability. Evaluation requires maintained application datasets and can itself incur cost. Synthetic scores in the prototype are not qualification evidence.

Required validation

Use held-out workload tests, excluded-destination tests and fallback checks. Compare actual task acceptance, total attempts and economics under the same workload.

Revisit trigger

Revisit thresholds when task requirements, drift or new models materially change the decision boundary.

Evidence Original design decision; evaluate against the stated acceptance gates.

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-021 · Source record

C1 disposition. Target only for live streaming. The candidate explicitly excludes streaming.
AP-ADR-021Make streaming completion and output enforcement explicitProposed
Area Architecture & runtimeSuggested owner Streaming runtime leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Once content is sent to a user, a later inspection cannot retract it. HTTP success can precede an incomplete stream or missing usage.

Alternatives considered

Always incremental output; always buffer; or per-contract incremental/buffered modes with a truthful enforcement guarantee.

Proposed decision

Use explicit streaming modes and one response state machine. Mandatory preventive output checks require buffering unless a proven safe segmentation contract exists. Stop transparent model fallback after user-visible output. Record incomplete outcomes and cancellation uncertainty separately from HTTP status.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Buffering increases memory and first-byte latency. Incremental mode may support detection/intervention rather than complete prevention. Some endpoints will remain unsupported under strict content requirements.

Required validation

Test split markers, malformed/partial tool arguments, slow readers, disconnects, missing trailers and inspector failures before and after first output.

Revisit trigger

Revisit segmented streaming only with a demonstrable safety boundary for the specific content and inspector.

Related decisions AP-ADR-005 AP-ADR-017 AP-ADR-018 AP-ADR-026

Evidence [R07]

Aperture target · Original ID AP-ADR-022 · Source record

C1 disposition. Response reuse is not qualified. LiteLLM namespace mechanisms require identity-derived partition tests. Related: RV-07
AP-ADR-022Default response reuse off and partition eligible caches by authorityProposed
Area Tenancy & securitySuggested owner Application data architectDate 8 October 2026

Context

Response reuse can leak tenant data or return an answer valid for a different authorization context. Similar wording does not establish equivalent business meaning.

Alternatives considered

Global exact/semantic caching; no cache ever; or opt-in contract-qualified reuse with explicit partitioning.

Proposed decision

Disable response caching initially. Enable exact reuse only for proven eligible tasks with tenant/principal authorization, contract/model/policy revision, request semantics and retrieval snapshot in the protected key. Keep stateful and side-effecting work out. Qualify semantic reuse separately with false-hit limits.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Lower cache-hit rates are acceptable when they preserve correctness. Invalidation and retention are real operating obligations. Provider prompt caching remains a different feature with its own data contract.

Required validation

Test foreign tenants and principals, changed retrieval grants, policy/model changes, stale entries, revoked callers and semantically misleading near-duplicates.

AP-ADR-023Bind stateful resources to tenant and provider ownershipProposed
Area Architecture & runtimeSuggested owner Stateful services leadDate 8 October 2026

Context

Files, response IDs, sessions and asynchronous jobs may belong to a specific provider account. An alias cannot safely migrate those objects by changing its target.

Alternatives considered

Forward arbitrary provider IDs; expose raw provider state without registry; or maintain a scoped resource registry and explicit affinity.

Proposed decision

Register creation owner, authorized workload/user scope, provider/account binding, lifecycle, expiry and deletion obligations for each stateful object. Reauthorize every retrieval, poll, cancellation and deletion. Require explicit reconstruction or completion before changing provider ownership.

Consequences and tradeoffs

Additional registry state and cleanup jobs are necessary. Portability is intentionally limited where upstream state is not transferable. The initial release can exclude protocols whose lifecycle is not qualified.

Required validation

Test cross-tenant IDs, key rotation, creator removal, alias changes, delayed job completion, duplicate cancellation and provider deletion failure.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when providers expose safe export/import or interoperable state contracts.

Context

A retrieval service using a broad gateway identity can return documents the end user is not allowed to see. Cache and embedding systems can magnify that error.

Alternatives considered

Gateway-wide retrieval credentials; application-managed retrieval only; or a separate approved broker preserving end-user scope and source ACLs.

Proposed decision

Keep business authorization at the retrieval/source system. A broker uses verified delegated identity, approved sources and explicit query/resource scope. Identity propagation and connector-specific permissions add complexity. Some sources cannot safely delegate and must remain application-managed. Context construction is still an application-quality responsibility.

Context

Execute tools in the model proxy; trust tool annotations; or use a separate execution boundary with explicit grants.

Place MCP/tool execution in a separate runtime and credential domain. Validate server/tool/operation grants, token audience, delegated identity, arguments and transaction idempotency. Context

Long-lived streams, slow readers and large contexts consume resources that a simple request-rate or CPU metric does not capture. Financial limits cannot guarantee latency fairness.

Alternatives considered

CPU-only autoscaling; unlimited queues; or bounded active-work capacity with tenant fairness and provider-aware scaling.

Proposed decision

Limit body size, active streams, queue wait, output, deadlines and per-tenant concurrency. Use weighted fair scheduling and scale on measured active work, saturation and admission latency. Revisit scheduling weights and limits from observed workload distributions and service objectives.

Context

Selecting Bedrock changes which infrastructure the organization operates, but does not settle application tenancy, workflow safety, spending discipline or portability. The reference architecture needs an accountable boundary before individual AWS capabilities or an additional gateway become default dependencies.

Options considered

  • Selected: native Bedrock clients behind an organization-owned application contract, minimizing mandatory infrastructure.
  • Conditional: a gateway when shared admission, multi-provider routing or migration compatibility justifies its operating cost.
  • Rejected: treating the complete application as AWS-operated because its model inference is managed.

Proposed decision

Adopt Bedrock as a managed inference and selected capability provider. Keep application authorization, business workflows, quality acceptance and financial policy under named customer ownership. Add a gateway only against a documented requirement and measure its incremental latency, failure modes and administrative burden. Publish the resulting responsibility boundary with each workload onboarding package.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Teams gain managed capabilities while retaining responsibility for their own data and actions.
  • A gateway becomes a separately justified deployment with its own availability and patching obligations.

Required validation

  • The service inventory assigns every request hop, persisted object and privileged action to a named operating role.
  • A native-client baseline and any gateway alternative are compared using identical functional, security and latency acceptance cases.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when additional providers, mandatory centralized admission or organizational isolation requirements make the current application boundary inadequate or unnecessarily expensive.

Publish supported API combinations and reject unsupported parameters at the application boundary. Document stream event handling for each admitted API. Propagate cancellation where supported, close abandoned transports promptly and retain enough metadata to reconcile uncertain completion. Familiar API shapes do not prove equal support for guardrails, capacity, streaming or recovery. Their value must be measured against a simpler prompting or retrieval baseline.

Options considered

  • Selected: separate qualification records for each customized or imported model artifact.
  • Rejected: automatic production trust because a job completed or an import was accepted.
  • Conditional: customization only after a demonstrated quality, latency or economics benefit over simpler alternatives.

Proposed decision

Record data rights, provenance, training configuration, artifact checksums where customer-accessible, evaluation results and supported serving contract. Isolate training and import roles from production invocation. Assess model-specific capacity, warm-up, retention and recovery requirements, including base-model lifecycle exposure. Promote through the same catalog and quality gates as other models, retaining a tested alternative where the custom path is unavailable.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Specialized models can improve a task while increasing data governance and deployment complexity.
  • Import portability remains bounded by supported formats and licenses; it is not a blanket promise of cross-service equivalence.

Required validation

  • Reproducibility checks identify the source data, artifact and training/import configuration for every production deployment.
  • The deployed artifact meets approved quality, capacity, policy and recovery tests, including denied artifact access and unavailable serving capacity.

Revisit trigger

Revisit when training data, base model, import support, license or serving mode changes, and when maintenance cost exceeds the demonstrated product benefit.

ADR-001Operate a shared enterprise gateway serviceProposed
Area Service contractSuggested owner Platform architecture leadDate 6 October 2026

Context

Several applications may need model access while identity, provider contracts and cost policy remain organization-wide concerns. Distributing these responsibilities across every application increases variation. A shared gateway introduces a dependency that requires an explicit operating owner and a bounded service contract.

Options considered

  • SDK in every application: simplest local integration, but each team owns credentials, governance and upgrades independently.
  • Shared gateway: selected for consistent controls and attribution, accepting an additional service and network dependency.
  • Gateway plus unrestricted direct access: rejected for production because policy coverage would depend on individual client behavior.

Proposed decision

Offer production model access through an organization-owned gateway endpoint. Applications retain business authorization, workflow orchestration and result validation. SDK use remains optional behind the gateway contract. Establish a service owner, incident route and onboarding policy before accepting production traffic, with direct provider access restricted to separately approved exceptions.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Central ownership can make model access and spend policy easier to change, while platform availability becomes part of every participating application's dependency model.
  • Provider credentials concentrate in a smaller operational boundary; that boundary needs stronger access management, maintenance discipline and a documented exception process.

Required validation

  • A representative application authenticates with its own workload identity, calls an approved alias and emits a trace attributable to its team.
  • An application lacking an approved exception cannot reach providers directly; disabling its gateway identity blocks further paid upstream calls.

Revisit trigger

Reassess when the application portfolio, operating capacity or existing enterprise API platform changes enough to alter the value of central ownership.

Context

A gateway's host runtime and native components are different architectural choices. The baseline must identify both, including components used automatically by its pinned artifact.   • Optional per-model Rust paths: keep off initially, then qualify their behavior and recovery separately against the baseline.
  • Standalone Axum gateway: evaluate as a distinct deployment; do not equate it with native modules inside the hosted gateway.

Proposed decision

Pin the supported stable Python-hosted gateway for baseline qualification and inventory every native component used automatically by that artifact. Consequences and tradeoffs

  • The Python-hosted baseline includes automatically loaded native dependencies, which belong in provenance, compatibility and operational review alongside the host application.

Required validation

  • The baseline artifact has a reviewed native-component inventory and passes the endpoint/control matrix with optional per-model Rust paths disabled.
  • Each optional path and standalone Axum candidate independently demonstrates expected stream, error, policy and accounting outcomes and its documented recovery mechanism.

Reopen when native-component maturity, application requirements or measured gateway resource costs create a concrete reason to change the qualified production execution path.

ADR-005Issue distinct workload keys with accountable ownershipProposed
Area Identity and trustSuggested owner Identity and access management leadDate 6 October 2026

Context

Production applications, individual developers and administrative automation have different lifecycles. Sharing one credential across them obscures attribution and makes revocation disruptive. Linking a durable production dependency to an employee's personal access can also create an avoidable outage during routine personnel changes.

Options considered

  • One shared master credential: rejected because compromise or rotation affects every application and grants excessive administrative authority.
  • Human-owned application keys: convenient initially, but rejected for durable services whose lifecycle exceeds a person's membership.
  • Scoped workload service accounts: selected for independent ownership, environment separation, model access and revocation without unrelated application disruption.

Proposed decision

Create one service account identity per production workload, environment and materially different privilege set. Associate it with a responsible team and bounded model access. Use separate human identities for development and administration. Prefer short-lived credentials where client support is proven, and inventory rotation, expiry and recovery ownership for remaining virtual keys.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Credential inventory grows, but incidents and application retirement can be handled without rotating every consumer or guessing which workload caused usage.
  • Service-account continuity must be balanced with ownership review so keys that survive staff departures do not become forgotten, indefinitely authorized assets.

Required validation

  • Revoking one workload identity stops its requests on every replica without interrupting another application's approved traffic.
  • Removing a human owner has the documented effect on personal keys while the team service account continues under a verified remaining owner.

Revisit trigger

Review when workload identity support improves, organizational ownership changes or a credential incident exposes a weakness in key scope or lifecycle.

ADR-006Validate JWT issuer, audience and entitlement claims explicitlyProposed
Area Identity and trustSuggested owner Identity security architectDate 6 October 2026

Context

A token can have a valid signature while targeting another application or carrying claims with different meanings. Multiple identity providers make these ambiguities more likely. Authentication must establish both who issued the token and why the gateway should accept its intended audience and permissions.

Options considered

  • Global JWKS configuration alone: rejected because cryptographic verification does not express the complete issuer, audience and entitlement boundary.
  • Explicit issuer-specific trust configuration: selected to bind signing keys and claim mappings to each approved identity provider.
  • Custom authentication code: reserve for unmet requirements because it adds privileged logic and a separate security maintenance obligation.

Proposed decision

Configure exact expected issuer and audience values, stable identity claims and explicit entitlement mappings. For an issuer allowlist, remove unintended global fallback paths. Define the permitted lifetime of cached signing keys during IdP outages. Treat caller-supplied metadata as descriptive unless it is independently authenticated and authorized for the asserted purpose.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Tokens for other applications are rejected even when the identity provider shares signing keys, reducing accidental trust across organizational services.
  • Identity-provider onboarding and key rotation require controlled tests; strict trust policy may trade some outage tolerance for clearer revocation and authentication boundaries.

Required validation

  • Reject wrong-audience, unknown-issuer, expired and insufficiently scoped tokens, including a correctly signed token issued for another application.
  • Rotate signing keys and interrupt JWKS retrieval; observed acceptance and rejection remain within the agreed cache lifetime and recovery policy.

Revisit trigger

Reopen when adding an identity provider, changing claim semantics or accepting a different availability-versus-revocation tradeoff for signing-key outages in production.

Keys, teams and organizations organize access, but applications may also exchange file IDs, sessions, cached outputs and tool resources. These objects can outlive an individual request. Isolation must cover every lookup and mutation, not merely the permission to invoke a model endpoint.

Derive the tenant context from validated identity and enforce it for keys, budgets, logs, files, sessions, caches and tools. Document inheritance and empty-list semantics before provisioning. ADR-009Separate encryption material from rotating access credentialsProposed
Area Identity and trustSuggested owner Secrets management leadDate 6 October 2026

Context

Access credentials should rotate routinely, while persisted encrypted values must remain readable throughout upgrades and recovery. Combining those purposes makes a simple credential replacement capable of disrupting stored provider configuration. The reference design needs separate ownership, backup and incident procedures for each secret category.

Options considered

  • Master key as both access and encryption material: rejected for new deployments because routine rotation becomes a data migration.
  • Dedicated stable salt plus rotating access secrets: selected, with restricted recovery handling and documented limitations on salt replacement.
  • External secret retrieval: use where useful, but evaluate integration entitlement and runtime availability rather than assuming it removes all local secret exposure.

Proposed decision

Set a dedicated strong salt before registering stored credentials and protect it independently from the master key. Rotate access credentials through their documented lifecycle. With a dedicated salt, change the master secret and restart replicas rather than using master-key re-encryption. Preserve an authorized recovery copy of encryption material alongside database recovery procedures.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Routine access-key rotation becomes simpler, but losing the stable encryption secret can make restored provider and tool credentials unusable.
  • A suspected salt compromise requires a planned credential re-registration or supported migration, and secret-manager availability becomes part of the recovery and startup design.

Required validation

  • Restore a database and its authorized salt into isolation, then prove stored model and tool credentials decrypt without exposing plaintext in logs.
  • Rotate master and provider credentials across replicas; old access fails while approved workloads continue after the documented rollout and recovery sequence.

Revisit trigger

Reopen for encryption-material disclosure, a mandatory rotation requirement or a vendor release that introduces a supported and recoverable in-place salt migration.

Define approved destination, credential and data-location sets for each model alias and integration. Restrict request-supplied routing overrides and enforce egress controls where practical, including redirects and private-address handling. Require fallbacks, mirrors, logs and guardrail services to satisfy the same data policy as the original route before they can receive content.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Policy remains meaningful during failures and debugging, but adding providers or changing endpoint hostnames may require coordinated network and governance work.
  • Egress restrictions can break discovery, token refresh or observability unexpectedly unless those dependencies are inventoried and tested alongside inference destinations.

Required validation

  • Synthetic credentials and sensitive markers never reach unapproved hosts through alternate routing fields, redirects, error handling or optional callback paths.
  • Provider failover and auxiliary-service failures preserve the declared regional policy, with observable rejection when no compliant destination remains.

Revisit trigger

Review when provider contracts, approved regions, network architecture or auxiliary integrations change the set of permitted data recipients and processing locations.

C1 disposition. Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
ADR-011Start with weighted routing among approved equivalent deploymentsProposed
Area Request executionSuggested owner Gateway reliability leadDate 6 October 2026

Context

Routing can optimize capacity, latency or cost, but extra logic introduces state and may change application behavior. Without a demonstrated need for adaptive selection, an understandable baseline helps attribute measured improvements or regressions to the routing strategy itself.

Options considered

  • Weighted selection within an approved alias: selected for a simple baseline that reflects known capacity and deployment eligibility.
  • Latency-, usage- or cost-adaptive routing: defer until representative measurements establish a benefit and state overhead is understood.
  • Unconstrained cheapest-model routing: rejected because lower price does not establish equivalent quality, capability, availability or data policy.

Proposed decision

Begin with simple-shuffle weighted selection across deployments that satisfy the same alias contract. Set weights from approved capacity allocations and validate them under realistic traffic. Keep cooldown and fallback eligibility explicit. Introduce adaptive or custom routing only through a measured experiment that preserves the alias's capability, cost and residency boundaries.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • The baseline is easier to reason about during incidents and provides a comparison point, but it may not achieve the lowest possible latency or cost.
  • Uneven workloads and provider throttling still require capacity planning; weights should not be mistaken for guaranteed throughput or strict provider quota enforcement.

Required validation

  • Sustained representative traffic produces the intended approximate distribution while every chosen deployment remains inside the approved alias and residency set.
  • A throttled or failed deployment leaves rotation as intended, recovers without oscillation and does not trigger an unapproved fallback.

Revisit trigger

Reopen when measured tail latency, utilization or cost shows a material problem that an evaluated alternative routing strategy can address.

C1 disposition. Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
ADR-012Assign one retry owner and an end-to-end deadlineProposed
Area Request executionSuggested owner Application reliability architectDate 6 October 2026

Context

Clients and gateways can independently retry requests, multiplying attempts, spending and latency. A timeout does not prove that upstream work never started. Retry policy must therefore reflect operation side effects, safe repetition and the client's total response deadline.

Options considered

  • Independent retries at every layer: rejected because attempt multiplication and cumulative deadlines become difficult to predict or explain.
  • Gateway-owned bounded retries: selected for approved transient failures, with clients following the published application-level recovery contract.
  • No retries anywhere: retain for unsafe operations, but reject as a universal policy where limited retry can recover transient failures.

Proposed decision

Make the gateway the primary retry owner for ordinary eligible inference calls. Publish one end-to-end deadline, a maximum attempt budget and retryable error classes. Disable redundant client retries where practical. Treat stateful submission, tool execution and already-committed streams separately, requiring evidence of safe repetition or explicit application recovery before another attempt.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Requests have a bounded latency and amplification envelope, but some transient failures will surface earlier than they would under unbounded layered retries.
  • Application teams must distinguish safe retry from duplicate side effects and may need idempotency or reconciliation beyond what a model gateway can provide.

Required validation

  • Inject provider throttling, connection failure and delayed responses; recorded upstream attempts and total latency stay within the declared request budget.
  • After partial stream delivery or an acknowledged side effect, retry behavior matches the endpoint contract and does not silently duplicate work.

Revisit trigger

Review when a provider changes failure semantics, client defaults change or a new operation introduces a different idempotency and deadline requirement.

ADR-013Specify streaming, disconnect and cancellation behaviorProposed
Area Request executionSuggested owner Streaming API engineering leadDate 6 October 2026

Context

Streaming changes when output becomes visible and how later failures can be reported. Long-lived requests retain resources and may continue consuming provider capacity after disconnect. Applications need explicit partial-output, timeout, usage and cancellation semantics for each approved transport.

Options considered

  • Transparent byte forwarding only: insufficient because clients also require error, accounting, cancellation and policy behavior across stream lifecycles.
  • Qualified streaming contract: selected with bounded connections, documented event shapes, disconnect handling and endpoint-specific completion accounting.
  • Buffer every response universally: reject where unnecessary because it removes streaming benefits and can create avoidable memory and latency costs.

Proposed decision

Define time to first output, idle timeout, total deadline, partial-error signaling and client-disconnect behavior for each streaming route. Propagate cancellation where supported and measure remaining upstream work. Preserve final usage when available without inventing missing usage. Enable full buffering only where required output policy justifies the latency and resource tradeoff.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Clients can handle incomplete responses deliberately, but some upstream protocols will provide weaker cancellation or usage evidence than others.
  • Long streams require concurrency and connection planning; cancellation success cannot be inferred solely from closing the client socket or returning a gateway error.

Required validation

  • Disconnect clients before output and midway through long streams; observe provider activity, resource release and accounting within an agreed operational bound.
  • Inject malformed events, idle stalls and mid-stream failures; clients receive the documented terminal outcome without duplicated or silently corrupted output.

Revisit trigger

Reopen when adding realtime or another streaming protocol, changing ingress limits or learning that cancellation and final-usage behavior differ by provider.

Area Request executionSuggested owner AI security policy leadDate 6 October 2026

Context

Content controls can run before dispatch, concurrently or after output, providing different guarantees once streamed bytes or tool side effects are visible. The organization must distinguish mandatory prevention from monitoring and verify the endpoint and payload shapes actually covered.

Options considered

  • Client-selected guardrails: reject for mandatory policy because callers can omit them or choose weaker request settings.
  • Explicit always-on preventive controls: selected for required input and output policy, accepting documented latency and availability costs.
  • Audit-only scanning: retain for monitoring and evaluation, but do not describe it as preventing content that was already delivered.

Proposed decision

Attach mandatory guards through controlled server policy. Run required input checks before provider dispatch and explicitly configure output buffering when content must be blocked before delivery. Define fail behavior for unavailable or unsupported guards. Qualify each endpoint, provider, stream and payload shape, including cache hits and tool results, before asserting preventive coverage.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Required policy can add latency and reject traffic during guardrail outages; the business owner must accept that behavior rather than assuming scanning is free.
  • Guardrails reduce specific exposure but do not replace resource authorization, application quality evaluation or safe handling of generated code, queries and tool arguments.

Required validation

  • A prohibited synthetic marker never reaches the provider or client on preventive paths, including markers split across stream chunks and cached responses.
  • Missing registration, timeout, unsupported payload and guardrail-service failure produce the chosen observable denial or explicitly approved monitoring-only outcome.

Revisit trigger

Review after provider or guardrail upgrades, changes in policy, unacceptable false-positive rates or introduction of an endpoint outside the qualified coverage matrix.

ADR-015Keep exact response caching off by default and tenant-partitionedProposed
Area Request executionSuggested owner Data platform security leadDate 6 October 2026

Context

Response caching retains content and may reuse answers under a different identity or policy context. TTL and encryption address different risks from authorization. The reference gateway should not persist payloads merely because a coordination or cache backend is available.

Options considered

  • Cache every supported call automatically: rejected until privacy, authorization, freshness and invalidation requirements are established for those workloads.
  • Explicitly approved exact caching: selected with server-derived partitioning, retention and a tested relationship to access and guardrail checks.
  • Provider prompt caching only: consider separately because it has different semantics, storage responsibility and contractual behavior from gateway response reuse.

Proposed decision

Set exact response caching to off by default. Enable it only for approved workloads with a documented data class, TTL and invalidation strategy. Derive partitioning from trusted tenant and policy context rather than accepting a client namespace as authority. Exclude side-effecting, resource-sensitive or freshness-critical requests unless their complete identity and state semantics are proven.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Initial costs may be higher, but content retention and cross-context reuse are restricted until the workload demonstrates a worthwhile and safe benefit.
  • Cache-hit responses still require the declared access and content controls; model, prompt, retrieval-data or policy changes can require invalidation beyond ordinary time expiry.

Required validation

  • Identical prompts from different tenants and privilege contexts cannot retrieve another context's cached output, including after policy or membership changes.
  • No-store and configured retention behave as documented, and cache-hit requests still execute every control required by their approved policy.

Revisit trigger

Reopen for a workload with measured repetition, acceptable freshness requirements and enough expected cost or latency savings to justify cache qualification.

ADR-016Evaluate semantic caching as a separate product decisionProposed
Area Request executionSuggested owner Application evaluation leadDate 6 October 2026

Context

Semantically similar requests can require different answers because dates, negation, quantities or permissions differ. Semantic caching therefore changes application behavior and needs workload-specific evidence beyond exact-match correctness. A universal similarity threshold cannot establish the acceptable substitution risk.

Options considered

  • Enable semantic caching with a generic similarity threshold: rejected because similarity alone is not a workload-specific correctness guarantee.
  • Workload-specific semantic experiment: selected only after exact-cache isolation and a labeled acceptance corpus exist.
  • No semantic caching: retain as the production default when correctness, privacy or freshness costs outweigh demonstrated savings.

Proposed decision

Keep semantic caching disabled in the reference rollout. For a candidate workload, define labeled equivalent and nonequivalent request pairs, tenant boundaries, freshness windows and tolerated error rates. Evaluate the embedding model, threshold and invalidation together. Approve only a bounded use case whose measured savings exceed the accepted quality and operational costs.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • The organization avoids silently changing answer semantics, while workloads with repetitive natural-language intent may initially miss a useful optimization.
  • Evaluation and monitoring become continuous responsibilities because changes to prompts, embeddings, corpus content and user behavior can invalidate an earlier similarity threshold.

Required validation

  • The labeled corpus covers negation, numerical changes, dates, identity and near-duplicate requests, with harmful cache substitutions below the approved threshold.
  • A controlled rollout measures actual savings, wrong-hit rate and freshness failures; disabling semantic reuse restores the baseline without deleting required durable state.

Revisit trigger

Review when exact caching leaves a material measured opportunity or when the workload, embedding model and acceptable substitution risk change substantially.

ADR-017Use PostgreSQL as durable governance authorityProposed
Area State and governanceSuggested owner Database platform leadDate 6 October 2026

Context

Governance needs durable identity, configuration and spending records across restarts and replicas. Ephemeral state can accelerate admission but cannot replace a recoverable record. Database absence and degradation therefore require deliberate operating policies, capacity planning and observable recovery behavior.

Options considered

  • DB-less proxy: rejected for the governed production service because durable keys, configuration and budget authority are required.
  • Managed PostgreSQL: selected for durable control records, backup, access restrictions and an established operational support model.
  • Application-owned external authority only: defer unless the organization deliberately replaces LiteLLM governance and validates every affected integration path.

Proposed decision

Require PostgreSQL for the production governance plane and manage it as a protected durable dependency. Use distinct runtime and migration privileges, private connectivity and verified transport encryption. Define retention and recovery for each major data category. Treat Redis admission state as coordinated operational state that must reconcile with durable records, not as a substitute for them.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • The design gains persistent administration and recovery capability, while database capacity, maintenance and availability become part of the platform's service obligation.
  • Connection limits and write contention can constrain gateway scaling; database schema and encrypted credential recovery must remain aligned with the deployed application version.

Required validation

  • A deployment gate rejects a governed configuration without its required database, and a restore proves keys, permissions and stored provider configuration are usable.
  • Representative concurrency stays within the allocated connection and write budget, with visible behavior when the database rejects or cannot serve requests.

Revisit trigger

Reassess if the organization externalizes governance, changes database operating strategy or demonstrates a bottleneck requiring a different durable-state design for production workloads.

Context

Workers need shared limits, invalidations and leadership even when response payloads are never cached. Coupling coordination to an optional performance cache can disable important governance state. Its clients, pools and failure behavior therefore need explicit configuration and independent observation.

  • Local memory in each worker: reject for a shared enforcement domain because counters and invalidations would depend on request placement.

Proposed decision

Configure HA Redis for coordination across each enforcement domain, with routing and payload caches managed separately. Keep coordination active when response caching is off. Do not infer shared virtual-key auth caching or a revocation bound from coordination_redis; qualify auth caching and invalidation separately. Required validation

  • Multiple workers honor the declared shared limit; warmed virtual-key caches on every worker enforce revocation within a separately agreed and measured bound.

Review when worker count, tenancy, cache volume or Redis failure evidence justifies different partitioning, durability or coordination technology for the production service.

ADR-019Reserve spending and fail closed on unverifiable budgetsProposed
Area State and governanceSuggested owner FinOps and platform controls leadDate 6 October 2026

Context

Concurrent requests can appear affordable when checks see only previously recorded spending. Outages and stale counters further weaken admission. The organization must choose its availability-versus-spend tradeoff and distinguish estimable token requests from operations whose complete cost is unknown.

Options considered

  • Recorded-spend checks alone: rejected for bounded production spending because concurrent work can be admitted before previous costs are recorded.
  • Reservation plus fail-closed verification: selected for governed workloads, with explicit estimation and dependency assumptions.
  • Availability-first admission during state failure: permit only as a separately bounded exception with an accountable owner and predefined financial exposure.

Proposed decision

Keep reservation enabled and use fail_closed_budget_enforcement for budget verification, with sensible output limits and current price metadata. Leave database fail-open mode disabled. Because missing or nonpositive estimates skip reservation even with that flag, reject such requests or apply a separately qualified admission rule. Define accepted overshoot exposure and separate controls for batch and media workloads.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Spending controls improve under concurrency and stale-state conditions, but verified admission can reject useful work during coordination or database failures.
  • Missing or nonpositive estimates bypass reservation rather than becoming protected automatically by fail-closed verification; estimation gaps and absent terminal usage need separate admission and reconciliation controls.

Required validation

  • Concurrent expensive requests, stale Redis restoration and database/Redis outages remain within the approved exposure bound and return the documented rejection classes.
  • Requests with missing, zero and negative cost estimates are rejected or demonstrably governed by the separate admission rule; completed and interrupted requests release reservations correctly.

Revisit trigger

Reopen when spending becomes contractual prepayment, new unpriced endpoints enter scope or observed outage cost changes the accepted availability tradeoff.

Configuration may arrive through files, environment variables and administrative APIs. Without ownership rules, a restart or UI edit can change effective behavior unexpectedly.   • File-owned global configuration with delegated dynamic fields: selected to combine reviewability with bounded team autonomy.

Own global route, model, security and dependency configuration through versioned files and reviewed secret references.   • A restart and fresh deployment reproduce all protected settings from versioned inputs, with expected handling of permitted dynamic state.
  • Differing writes and deletion of file-owned settings are rejected; delegated fields and separately handled resource lists retain their documented persistence and propagation behavior.

Promote an immutable release manifest containing image digests, configuration revisions and migration identity. Run the acceptance corpus in staging and use a controlled traffic increase.   • Keep audit solely in the mutable application database: insufficient where tamper resistance, investigation continuity or independent retention is required.

Proposed decision

Capture administrative changes with authenticated actor, operation, target, time and a suitably redacted change description. Export to a separately restricted audit destination and assign retention through organizational policy. Permit attribution overrides only for specifically authorized delegation. Verify delivery and gaps without claiming tamper-proof or complete history merely because an audit feature is enabled.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Investigations can separate administrative changes from inference events, while retention, access reviews and delivery monitoring create a distinct operational responsibility.
  • Audit data may contain sensitive configuration or identifiers and must be minimized; an unavailable audit sink needs an agreed response for high-impact administrative operations.

Required validation

  • Key, role, model and budget changes produce attributable records that a normal workload caller cannot forge through request metadata or headers.
  • A controlled export outage exposes a detectable gap or retry state, and authorized reviewers can retrieve retained records after application database restoration.

Revisit trigger

Review when regulatory retention, delegation workflows or incident evidence requires stronger durability, integrity controls or a different administrative failure policy.

C1 disposition. Historical product-specific proposal. No transfer of product behavior, license entitlement or acceptance to Aperture. Revalidate time-sensitive claims before a new procurement or deployment decision.
ADR-027Apply database schemas through one controlled migration jobProposed
Area Operations and resilienceSuggested owner Database release ownerDate 6 October 2026

Context

Multiple replicas starting simultaneously should not independently decide how to change durable shared state. A schema change also needs privileges different from routine request processing. The release process must coordinate migrations, application compatibility and recovery while keeping schema mutation out of ordinary pod startup.

Options considered

  • Migrate from every serving pod: rejected because rollout concurrency and elevated runtime privilege complicate control and failure recovery.
  • One version-matched migration job: selected as a gated release operation with explicit privileges and backup preparation.
  • Manual ad hoc database edits: rejected as a normal path because drift is difficult to reproduce and reconcile with application migration history.

Proposed decision

Disable automatic schema updates on serving instances and run one controlled migration job for the shared database. Match the job to the promoted application release, inspect changes and establish backup/recovery readiness first. Prevent application rollout when migration fails. Validate mixed-version compatibility or choose a coordinated maintenance sequence when it cannot be assured.

Consequences and tradeoffs

  • Schema changes have one observable owner and gate, but a failed migration can legitimately delay the release until recovery is understood.
  • A successful migration command does not establish absence of schema drift or safe downgrade; those assumptions need separate review and evidence.

Required validation

  • Simultaneous deployment attempts cannot run conflicting migrations, and failure of the migration job prevents the new serving version from receiving traffic.
  • A restored database and chosen recovery artifact successfully process required transactions after a deliberately failed or incompatible staging migration.

Revisit trigger

Reassess for a breaking schema change, multiple regional release pipelines or tooling that changes migration locking and application compatibility guarantees.
